A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LAOF with the same authors, framework and core experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated and added content to be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIBERO and PROCGEN experiments, including downstream performance, representation evaluations and architectural and sensitivity ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds LIBERO-Plus evaluations, an ARX-R5 robot experiment and motion–action correlation analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix B.2 changes the stated continuous latent model from a plain autoencoder to a standard VAE with KL weight 1e-6. New Appendix A.2 also evaluates LAOF-Δ, replacing optical flow with consecutive DINOv2 feature differences. The core IDM/FDM/flow-decoder pipeline remains unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates simulated LIBERO manipulation and PROCGEN games. v2 adds LIBERO-Plus lighting and background perturbations and a physical ARX-R5 drawer-opening, sponge-retrieval and placement task with five background settings. These substantially extend the environments and test scenarios.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged. New Tables 4–5 explicitly compare RAFT, SEA-RAFT and DINOv2 feature differences, including the LAOF-Δ control. SEA-RAFT was already described as tested in v1 Section 7, so its tabulation expands an existing comparison rather than establishing first use.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 changes the reported PROCGEN image/flow storage resolution from 64×64 to 256×256. Added protocols specify 2M-sample mixture training for the robustness comparison, PCA from 768 to 50 dimensions before CCA on 200K sampled observations per benchmark, Gaussian-noise controls, and 20 evaluations per method for the robot task. Existing main-text splits, budgets and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.2 adds controlled lighting/background robustness evaluations and examines whether motion-source choice and motion–action alignment explain downstream performance. Tables 4–5 compare optical-flow estimators and feature differences across environments. The earlier architectural ablations and lambda sensitivity analysis remain, with the latter moved from A.2 to A.3.

E5.justification: Beyond the retained Pearson-correlation analysis, v2 adds PCA-based CCA estimation of motion-feature associations with physical actions and Gaussian noise. The original five-seed protocol and mean/standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged. No confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: New Tables 4–5 report correlation estimates and robustness, robot and motion-source results. LIBERO-Plus scores are 43.4 for LAPO, 63.5 for LAOF-R and 68.3 for LAOF-S; robot successes are 14/20, 18/20 and 18/20, respectively. Tables 1–3 and earlier plots retain their results. Table 5's LIBERO/PROCGEN LAPO and LAOF-R values are rounded aggregates of existing results, not cross-version gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical spaces, assumptions and equations in Sections 3–4 are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and the added empirical CCA analysis introduces no formal derivation or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introduction contributions and Section 5.2 conclusions retain the same substantive claims about optical-flow constraints, sparse-label stability, downstream performance and decoder placement. The new appendix supplies additional evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 7 removes the explicit optical-flow generalization limitation and changes applicability from mainly eye-off-hand scenarios to only eye-to-hand scenarios, while expanding future directions to egocentric videos, cross-embodiment and camera motion. Appendix A.2 links stronger motion–action alignment to robustness. Appendix B.2 removes the earlier argument against VAE priors.

D1.justification: v2 documents the ARX-R5 platform, 20 Hz collection, 100 trajectories, 47,989 samples and five backgrounds, plus the CCA feature-processing dimensions. It revises storage/model specifications and supplies the VAE KL weight. The existing hyperparameter table, now Table 6, and code-access URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to UMI, FastUMI-100K, LIBERO-Plus, DreamDojo and Learning Latent Action World Models in the Wild. It refines the FlowVLA comparison around discretization and language supervision. The broader research positioning remains intact; reference renumbering and publication updates are not substantive additions.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the introduction, related work, limitations and model setup. v2 inserts Appendix A.2, moves and expands the acknowledgment before the references, and adds a corresponding-author note while retaining the main narrative structure. FlowVLA's bibliography title is reduced to 'C.'

P2.justification: v2 adds a robot optical-flow visualization as Figure 8 and new Tables 4–5. Existing figures remain visually unchanged; the lambda plot becomes Figure 9 and the hyperparameter table becomes Table 6. The GOAL table heading is corrected, and pagination and reference/appendix layout are updated without a broad redesign.

improvement.justification: The new robustness tests, physical robot experiment and motion–action analysis strengthen evidence for LAOF's central claims beyond v1's simulated benchmarks. The gain is limited by one robot task with 20 evaluations per method and unexplained VAE/resolution revisions alongside unchanged main results. The CCA claim of 200K samples per benchmark also leaves sampling from the 47,989 collected robot observations unclear.
